title: Automated counterproposal generator with SQ context and risk heatmap
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Build an in-console tool that drafts redline counterproposals for MSAs/DPAs by synthesizing the incoming contract redlines and the customer Security Questionnaire (SQ) responses, and surfaces a visual risk heatmap and recommended approval tier. The generator should produce: (1) an editable counterproposal summary with clause-level rationale, (2) suggested liability/indemnity language tuned to customer size and revenue, and (3) an approval path and suggested pricing margin impact. Goal: reduce manual legal drafting for repeatable concession patterns and empower Sales with defensible counteroffers.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Sofia Patel: Initial proposal drafted after Sales & Legal sync. Problem: deals slow down waiting for Legal to manually compose counterproposals; SQ context often not surfaced to Sales. Proposed MVP: clause templates + risk heatmap + recommended approval tier.

2026-03-03 - Ethan Walker: Scoped MVP to support top 12 most common redline clauses (indemnity, liability cap, data processing addendum specifics, escrow, termination for convenience). Will rely on existing SQ parsing pipeline and clause fingerprinting service (research task).

2026-03-04 - Legal (R. Kim): Reviewed list of clauses; requested explicit escape hatch for Legal to edit generated language and audit log of suggestions. Must include citation to precedent clauses and past concession data.

2026-03-05 - Eng (Maya Lopez): POC estimate: 8 points. We can reuse clause templates from contract library and map SQ flags to risk adjustments. Required: endpoint to fetch customer SQ responses and normalized score, and backend rule engine to produce draft language.

2026-03-06 - Sales Ops (D. Nguyen): Suggested sales surface: one-click accept-to-send to counterparty and a 'fast-track' checkbox that auto-routes to commercial counsel when margin impact < X%. Need guardrails for enterprise deals > $250k ARR.

2026-03-08 - PM (Sofia): Added acceptance criteria: generated counterproposal should include (a) clause diff summary, (b) heatmap (low/med/high) per clause with rationale, (c) recommended approval tier and expected pricing impact, (d) link to precedent PR/notes. UX must allow inline edits and preserve audit history.

2026-03-09 - Legal (R. Kim): Security review required flagged for data handling clauses. Also flagged that some customers include third-party indemnities — generator must detect and escalate automatically.

2026-03-10 - Eng (Maya): Identified dependency on clause-fingerprint-service (ENG-24812) and SQ normalizer (ENG-30291). Will produce API contract doc and a skeleton GraphQL endpoint for PM/Console to call.

2026-03-10 - PM (Sofia): Next steps: 1) finalize clause templates and precedence mapping with Legal, 2) design Console mockups with Design, 3) engineering spike to validate automated language quality on 50 historical redlines. Owner: Ethan. Target: spike complete by 2026-03-24.
notes: Trade-offs: fully automated language risks accuracy; MVP will be conservative and favor escalation over risky auto-approval.
Metrics to track: time-to-counterproposal, % deals closed within 14 days, # of escalations to Legal, post-deal claim rate tied to concession types.
Privacy: generated drafts may include customer-sensitive SQ responses; ensure drafts are stored in encrypted audit ledger and access-controlled.
Design considerations: present heatmap as compact row with color and short rationale; allow expansion to see precedent clauses and scoring factors.
Potential follow-ups: expand to include pricing slider to simulate margin impact, A/B test 'fast-track' acceptance vs manual Legal review on mid-market deals.
